title: Reliability Initiative: SLI Commitment Tracker & Adaptive Allocation Protocol
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build an initiative-level tracker and decision protocol that converts SLI telemetry and error-budget burn into recommended allocation changes, proactive rollbacks, and stakeholder notifications. The tracker surfaces per-initiative SLI attainment, projected error-budget runway, and suggested actions (throttle rollout, pause experiments, increase dedicated capacity) to PMs and RTEs.
objectives: Create a dashboard that shows initiative-level SLI attainment and 90/95/99th percentile error-budget runway projections
Define and automate a three-tier action matrix (advisory, recommended, required) tied to error-budget burn rates
Integrate with Console rollouts API to surface recommended throttles/canary pauses as one-click actions
Provide audit trail for allocation decisions and post-mortem notes to feed quarterly OKR reviews
success_criteria: Dashboard available in Console under Reliability > Initiatives with data refresh <= 5 minutes
Action matrix executed in >= 90% of simulated burn scenarios in the staging runbook
At least two teams use the one-click pause/throttle action in a real canary deployment before due date
Stakeholder survey shows > 80% confidence in suggested actions (PMs/Eng leads) after first month
scope: IN: initiative-level aggregation of per-route SLIs, burn-rate projections, and recommended actions
IN: Console UI, webhook/action integration with rollouts and incident channels
OUT: automatic traffic migration between regions (separate infra effort)
OUT: changes to underlying kernel selection or quantization profiles (runtime team scope)
decisions: Use 30-day rolling window for baseline SLI and 12-hour burn-rate window for runway projection
Three-tier action matrix adopted: Advisory (notify), Recommended (email + Console badge), Required (block rollout, create incident)
Initial rollout will support latency and error-rate SLIs; availability/throughput to be added in phase 2
tradeoffs: Short burn windows surface volatility; chose 12-hour window to prioritize responsiveness over stability
Aggressive automatic required actions reduce availability of experiments but lower production risk
Consolidating SLI aggregation at initiative level may hide route-level hotspots; we will surface top contributing routes in the UI
risks_mitigation: Risk: noisy telemetry causing false positives —> Mitigation: require sustained breach across two consecutive 12-hour windows before Required action
Risk: teams override recommendations without audit —> Mitigation: make overrides require justification and capture in audit trail
Risk: integration latency with rollouts API —> Mitigation: add a safe dry-run mode and preflight checks
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Jan): Design workshop with Console, Runtime, and SRE to align on data model and APIs
Phase 1 (Feb): Build backend aggregator, sample dataset ingestion, and staging dashboard; run simulated burn scenarios
Phase 2 (Mar): Integrate with rollouts one-click actions and pilot with two product teams on Dedicated workloads
Phase 3 (Apr): Expand supported SLIs and promote to GA with docs and playbook trainings
monitoring_and_alerting: New telemetry stream: initiative_sli_attainment{initiative, sli, window} to metrics cluster
Alert rule: advisory when projected runway < 7 days, recommended when < 72 hours, required when < 24 hours and sustained
On-call routing: send advisory to #reliability-advisory, required to on-call SRE and PM pager
